result.title: Radioactive Feedback: Tracing Models Trained by Label-Only LLM Supervision
result.summary: Conventional distillation transfers capability through teacher-generated demonstrations. LLM-as-a-Judge knowledge distillation offers a distinct and increasingly practical alternative. In the label-only variant studied here, the student generates every response and improves from scalar scores alone. Prior work shows that this non-demonstrative feedback can improve student capability, but it creates a fundamentally different provenance problem. No teacher-generated answer enters the student's training set, so any evaluator-specific trace must pass through a low-bandwidth reward signal rather than copied text. Existing watermarks and distillation detectors do not cover this score-only channel. We introduce Radioactive Feedback, which encodes a registered pattern of behavioral preferences in the rewards themselves. The evaluator applies bounded pointwise adjustments to quality-qualified responses, allowing repeated optimization to transfer the pattern to a student trained by another party. Experiments on code and mathematics show that the registered preferences transfer through scores alone and across datasets, enabling black-box detection against a fixed reference pool.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究仅有标量评分、无教师示范的 LLM-as-a-Judge 蒸馏设定，提出「Radioactive Feedback」：评估方在质量达标回复上加有界微调，把注册的行为偏好编码进奖励，使其经反复优化转移到他人训练的模型中，并在代码与数学任务上展示跨数据集的偏好转移与黑盒检测。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作把低带宽标量奖励当作可承载结构化偏好的监督通道，可能可供核查 LVR 中纯结果型奖励能否塑造 latent 推理状态的结构与内容，以及监督信号的可追溯性与贡献分配问题；但其任务均为文本代码与数学，向多模态推理状态的迁移仍待核查。
